posts.content_md:
Has/is anyone doing any work with LiNbO3?

Can a single beam reflection hologram be made in it?

What is the maxium thickness for a reflection hologram?

What is the best dopant? Iron?

Is there anyting else you could tell us about working with it?

I think it would be great to be able to record a reflection hologram in this crystal and then do a proximity copy into DCG.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I have read a little about Fe doped LiNbO3. It appears to take lots of energy, it is only available in small sizes, it is very expensive and it is mainly used in holographic memory research where a hologram is written into many planes in a cube sized crystal. If I remember right reading the data erases it a little each time so a refresh cycle is added.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Maybe it is not LiNbO3. I was thinking of a non linear crystal that gets erased with an electrical current not light. Is that a differently doped LiNbO3 or a different material all together?
